description: A study of cooperative societies in Tanzania, covering their meaning, history, principles, types, formation, management, advantages and disadvantages, and their role in national development.

options.text: A voluntary association of people who join together to meet their common economic, social and cultural needs through a jointly owned and democratically controlled enterprise
A company owned by a single wealthy shareholder seeking maximum profit
A government department that controls all trade in a country
A group of competing businesses that fix prices to cheat customers

mcq.explanation: A cooperative society is a voluntary, self-help association where members pool resources to meet shared needs and own and control the enterprise democratically.

mcq.questionText: Which principle states that each member of a cooperative society has only one vote regardless of the number of shares held?

options.text: Voluntary and open membership
Democratic member control (one member one vote)
Concern for community
Autonomy and independence

mcq.explanation: Under democratic member control, voting is on the basis of one member one vote, unlike companies where votes depend on the number of shares held.

options.text: Savings and Credit Cooperative Society
Sale and Cash Cooperative Service
Savings Account Central Cooperative System
Society of Agricultural Cash Crop Owners

mcq.explanation: SACCOS means Savings and Credit Cooperative Society, which collects members' savings and provides loans to them at fair interest rates.

mcq.questionText: A cooperative formed by coffee farmers in Kilimanjaro to sell their crop collectively is an example of a:

options.text: Consumer cooperative
Producer or marketing cooperative
Housing cooperative
Savings and credit cooperative

mcq.explanation: Marketing or producer cooperatives help members sell their produce (e.g. coffee, cotton, cashew) jointly to obtain better prices and bargaining power.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is a recognised cooperative principle?

options.text: Maximisation of profit for outside investors
Education, training and information for members
Secrecy of all accounts from members
Membership restricted by tribe or religion

mcq.explanation: Cooperatives provide education, training and information to members, elected officers and employees so they can contribute effectively to the society.

mcq.questionText: The supreme decision-making body of a cooperative society is the:

options.text: Manager
Management committee
General meeting of members
Registrar of cooperatives

mcq.explanation: The general meeting, where all members participate, is the highest authority; it elects the committee and approves major decisions.

mcq.questionText: A consumer cooperative society mainly aims to:

options.text: Buy goods in bulk and sell them to members at fair prices
Process members' coffee for export
Build houses for members only
Lend money to non-members at high interest

mcq.explanation: Consumer cooperatives purchase goods in bulk directly from producers or wholesalers and sell them to members, eliminating middlemen and lowering prices.

mcq.questionText: Which body is responsible for registering cooperative societies in Tanzania?

options.text: Bank of Tanzania
The Registrar of Cooperative Societies (Cooperative Development Commission)
Tanzania Revenue Authority
Business Registrations and Licensing Agency (BRELA) only

mcq.explanation: Cooperatives are registered by the Registrar under the Tanzania Cooperative Development Commission (TCDC), giving them a legal certificate of registration.

mcq.questionText: Surplus (profit) earned by a cooperative society is usually distributed to members in the form of:

options.text: Dividends based on the number of shares only
Patronage refund based on how much each member traded with the society
Bonuses paid to the manager
Donations to political parties

mcq.explanation: Cooperatives mainly return surplus to members in proportion to their transactions (patronage), reflecting member economic participation rather than share-based profit.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is a major advantage of cooperative societies?

options.text: They are controlled by a few rich investors
They encourage saving and give members access to affordable credit and goods
They eliminate the need for any record keeping
They pay no attention to member welfare

mcq.explanation: Cooperatives promote thrift, provide cheaper goods and affordable loans, and pool members' resources for mutual benefit.

mcq.questionText: Which is commonly cited as a disadvantage or problem of cooperative societies in Tanzania?

options.text: Poor management and lack of skilled, trained personnel
Too much capital from too many wealthy owners
Members each having too many votes
Complete absence of any members

mcq.explanation: Many cooperatives suffer from weak, untrained management, embezzlement and inadequate capital, which limit their efficiency and growth.

mcq.questionText: The principle of 'cooperation among cooperatives' means that cooperative societies should:

options.text: Compete fiercely and try to close one another down
Work together through local, national and international structures to strengthen the movement
Merge with private companies for profit
Avoid contact with other cooperatives

mcq.explanation: Cooperatives serve members best and strengthen the movement by working together through unions, apex bodies and international links.

mcq.questionText: A primary cooperative society differs from a cooperative union mainly because a primary society:

options.text: Has individual people as its members
Is owned by the government
Cannot be registered legally
Has other cooperatives as its members

mcq.explanation: A primary cooperative is made up of individual members, while a cooperative union is a secondary society whose members are primary cooperatives.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following best describes the principle of 'autonomy and independence'?

options.text: Cooperatives are self-help organisations controlled by their members and remain independent even when dealing with governments or other bodies
Cooperatives must always be fully controlled by the central government
Members are forbidden from leaving the cooperative
Cooperatives may never enter agreements with banks

mcq.explanation: Autonomy and independence means cooperatives are self-governing; when they raise capital or deal with outsiders they do so on terms that preserve member control.

mcq.questionText: In a cooperative society, the day-to-day running of operations is the responsibility of the:

options.text: General meeting
Manager and staff appointed by the committee
Registrar of cooperatives
Auditors only

mcq.explanation: The general meeting sets policy and elects the committee; the committee appoints a manager who, with staff, handles daily operations.

fib.questionText: A _____ cooperative society collects savings from members and gives them loans, and is commonly known in Tanzania as a SACCOS.
fib.explanation: Savings and credit cooperatives (SACCOS) mobilise members' savings and lend to members at reasonable interest rates.

fib.questionText: Under the cooperative principle of democratic control, each member has one _____ regardless of the number of shares held.
fib.explanation: The one member one vote rule ensures equal control among members, unlike companies where voting depends on shareholding.

fib.questionText: Cooperative societies that help farmers sell crops such as coffee, cotton and cashew are called producer or _____ cooperatives.
fib.explanation: Marketing cooperatives collect and sell members' produce jointly to obtain better prices and stronger bargaining power.

fib.questionText: The highest authority in a cooperative society is the _____ meeting of all members.
fib.explanation: The general meeting elects the management committee, approves budgets and makes the most important decisions.

fib.questionText: A cooperative society obtains its legal status after being _____ by the Registrar of Cooperative Societies.
fib.explanation: Once registered, a cooperative becomes a body corporate with a legal personality separate from its members.

fib.questionText: A cooperative whose members are other primary cooperatives is called a cooperative _____.
fib.explanation: A cooperative union is a secondary society formed by primary cooperatives to provide services such as marketing and processing.

fib.questionText: The committee that is elected by members to oversee and direct the affairs of a cooperative is called the management _____.
fib.explanation: The management committee (board) is elected at the general meeting and is responsible for supervising the society on members' behalf.

fib.questionText: Surplus shared with members according to how much business each did with the society is known as a patronage _____.
fib.explanation: A patronage refund returns surplus to members in proportion to their transactions, reflecting member economic participation.

fib.questionText: The principle of voluntary and open membership means cooperatives are open to all persons able to use their services without social, racial, political, religious or _____ discrimination.
fib.explanation: Membership is voluntary and open to all willing and able persons without discrimination, including on the basis of gender.

fib.questionText: A type of cooperative formed so that members can pool funds to build or buy homes is called a _____ cooperative.
fib.explanation: Housing cooperatives help members access land and build or own houses by pooling resources and obtaining group loans.

tf.questionText: In a cooperative society, voting is based on the number of shares a member holds.
tf.explanation: Cooperatives follow one member one vote regardless of shares; share-based voting applies to companies, not cooperatives.

tf.questionText: SACCOS in Tanzania mainly provide savings and credit services to their members.
tf.explanation: Savings and Credit Cooperative Societies collect members' savings and lend money to members at fair interest.

tf.questionText: Membership of a genuine cooperative society is voluntary and open to all who can use its services.
tf.explanation: Voluntary and open membership is a core principle; no one is forced to join and membership is non-discriminatory.

tf.questionText: Coffee and cotton marketing cooperatives are examples of consumer cooperatives.
tf.explanation: Coffee and cotton cooperatives are producer/marketing cooperatives; consumer cooperatives buy and sell goods to members.

tf.questionText: A cooperative society can be registered and obtain a separate legal personality.
tf.explanation: After registration by the Registrar, a cooperative becomes a body corporate able to own property and sue or be sued.

tf.questionText: The manager of a cooperative society is always the highest authority, above the general meeting.
tf.explanation: The general meeting is the highest authority; the manager is an employee responsible for day-to-day operations.

tf.questionText: Poor management, embezzlement and inadequate capital are common problems facing cooperatives in Tanzania.
tf.explanation: These weaknesses have undermined many Tanzanian cooperatives and reduced members' confidence in them.

tf.questionText: Cooperatives are required to discriminate against members on the basis of religion or tribe.
tf.explanation: Open membership forbids discrimination on grounds such as religion, tribe, gender or politics.

tf.questionText: Cooperative societies have played an important role in marketing Tanzania's cash crops and improving rural incomes.
tf.explanation: Crop marketing cooperatives have helped farmers sell produce, gain better prices and contribute to rural development.

tf.questionText: Education and training of members and officers is one of the recognised cooperative principles.
tf.explanation: Cooperatives provide education and training so that members and elected officers can run the society effectively.

summary.correctAnswer: A cooperative society is a voluntary association of people who come together to meet their common economic, social and cultural needs through a jointly owned and democratically controlled enterprise.
summary.explanation: This captures the self-help, voluntary, jointly owned and democratically controlled nature of cooperatives.

summary.questionText: List any four principles of cooperative societies.
summary.correctAnswer: Voluntary and open membership; democratic member control (one member one vote); member economic participation; and education and training of members. (Others: autonomy and independence, cooperation among cooperatives, concern for community.)
summary.explanation: These are drawn from the internationally recognised cooperative principles applied in Tanzania.

summary.questionText: Name and briefly describe three types of cooperative societies.
summary.correctAnswer: Consumer cooperatives buy goods in bulk and sell to members cheaply; producer/marketing cooperatives sell members' crops such as coffee and cotton jointly; and savings and credit cooperatives (SACCOS) collect savings and lend to members.
summary.explanation: These three types are common in Tanzania along with housing and service cooperatives.

summary.questionText: Outline the steps in forming and registering a cooperative society.
summary.correctAnswer: Interested people hold a meeting and agree to form the society; they elect leaders and draft by-laws; they collect shares and entrance fees; they apply to the Registrar of Cooperative Societies with the required documents; and after approval the society is registered and receives a certificate of registration.
summary.explanation: Registration gives the society legal status and the right to operate as a body corporate.

summary.questionText: Describe the management structure of a cooperative society.
summary.correctAnswer: The general meeting of all members is the supreme body; it elects a management committee to oversee the society; the committee appoints a manager and staff who handle the day-to-day operations.
summary.explanation: This three-tier structure separates ownership (members), governance (committee) and operations (manager).

summary.questionText: State four advantages of cooperative societies.
summary.correctAnswer: They encourage saving and provide affordable credit; they sell goods to members at fair prices; they give farmers stronger bargaining power for their produce; and they promote unity, self-reliance and member welfare.
summary.explanation: These benefits arise from pooling members' resources and eliminating exploitative middlemen.

summary.questionText: State four disadvantages or problems of cooperative societies.
summary.correctAnswer: Poor and untrained management; embezzlement and dishonesty among leaders; inadequate capital; and slow decision-making due to the need to consult members.
summary.explanation: These weaknesses have limited the efficiency and growth of many cooperatives in Tanzania.

summary.questionText: Explain the role of cooperative societies in the development of Tanzania.
summary.correctAnswer: Cooperatives market cash crops such as coffee, cotton and cashew, raising rural incomes; SACCOS provide affordable credit and encourage saving; they create employment, supply goods at fair prices, promote self-reliance and contribute to national economic growth.
summary.explanation: Cooperatives have historically been central to rural marketing and financial inclusion in Tanzania.

summary.questionText: Distinguish between a primary cooperative society and a cooperative union.
summary.correctAnswer: A primary cooperative society is formed by individual people as its members, while a cooperative union is a secondary society whose members are primary cooperatives that join together for stronger marketing, processing and services.
summary.explanation: This shows the difference in membership and level within the cooperative movement.

summary.questionText: Explain the principle of 'member economic participation'.
summary.correctAnswer: Members contribute equitably to, and democratically control, the capital of the cooperative; part of that capital is usually common property, and members receive limited returns on shares while surpluses are used to develop the society or returned to members as patronage refunds.
summary.explanation: This principle stresses fair member contribution and benefit rather than profit for outside investors.

hoq.questionText: A group of cashew farmers in Mtwara sells their nuts individually to private traders and constantly receives low prices because buyers set the prices. Which action would best apply cooperative principles to solve their problem?

options.text: Each farmer should stop growing cashew and migrate to town
Form a marketing cooperative to bulk and sell the cashew jointly, increasing their bargaining power
Sell all the cashew to a single private trader at any price he offers
Ask the government to take over their farms permanently

hoq.explanation: A marketing cooperative pools members' produce so they sell collectively, gaining stronger bargaining power and better prices, which directly applies cooperative principles.

hoq.questionText: A newly formed SACCOS finds that a few leaders with the most shares are trying to control all decisions and outvote other members. Which cooperative principle is being violated and how should it be corrected?

options.text: Concern for community; correct it by donating profits to charity
Democratic member control; correct it by applying one member one vote regardless of shares
Education and training; correct it by closing the SACCOS
Voluntary membership; correct it by forcing all to buy more shares

hoq.explanation: Allowing control by the largest shareholders breaches democratic member control; the remedy is enforcing one member one vote so all members have equal say.

hoq.questionText: A cooperative union has been losing members' trust because of repeated embezzlement, weak records and untrained leaders. Which combination of measures would most effectively address these problems?

options.text: Hide the accounts from members and stop holding general meetings
Train and educate members and leaders, employ a qualified manager, keep proper records and ensure regular auditing
Increase entrance fees and ignore the missing money
Convert the union into a private company owned by the chairman

hoq.explanation: Strengthening education and training, hiring competent management, maintaining proper records and regular auditing directly tackle the causes of poor management and embezzlement while upholding cooperative principles.
